section_1.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: Conditional Probability
section_1.content: Briefly revisit the idea of 'updating' information. Define P(A|B) as the probability of A given that B has occurred, visualized as zooming into a subset of a Venn diagram.
section_1.example: A bowl has 5 red apples and 5 green pears. If you pick a fruit and it is red, the 'universe' of possibilities shrinks from 10 to just the 5 red fruits.

section_2.title: Defining Independence
section_2.content: Introduce independence: Two events are independent if the occurrence of one doesn't change the probability of the other. Visually, P(A|B) = P(A).
section_2.example: Flipping a coin (Event A) and rolling a die (Event B). No matter what the coin shows, the die remains equally likely to land on any side.

section_3.title: The Core: Bayes' Theorem
section_3.content: Introduce the theorem as a bridge between 'what we know' (prior) and 'new evidence' (likelihood). Use a formula graphic where terms are color-coded: P(H|E) = [P(E|H) * P(H)] / P(E).
section_3.example: A medical test (Evidence) for a rare disease (Hypothesis). Even if the test is 99% accurate, the low prevalence (Prior) changes the interpretation of a positive result.

section_4.title: Application: The Detective Robot
section_4.content: Apply the theorem to a dynamic scenario. Show how a robot updates its 'belief' about its location after receiving sensor data. Link the concept of 'updating' back to the previous sections.
section_4.example: A robot senses a wall. Using Bayes' Theorem, it combines its previous location estimate (Prior) with the sensor reading (Evidence) to calculate a new, more accurate position (Posterior).

section_5.title: Synthesis & Summary
section_5.content: Summary slide: Independence means information is irrelevant; Bayes' Theorem means information is transformative. A final visual summary comparing the two.
section_5.example: Independence = Parallel paths; Bayes' = A feedback loop that refines our understanding of the world.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Application: The Detective Robot", [
            "Robots use Bayes to localize themselves.",
            "Sensors provide the new evidence.",
            "Beliefs update to match reality.",
            "A more accurate position is calculated.",
            "Probability is a dynamic estimation process."
        ])
        
        # Create grid representation of robot locations
        grid_group = VGroup()
        for pos in self.grid.values():
            dot = Dot(pos, color=WHITE, radius=0.1)
            grid_group.add(dot)
        self.add(grid_group)
        
        # Indicator for most likely location
        target_dot = Dot(self.grid["C3"], color=YELLOW, radius=0.15)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(FadeIn(grid_group))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        # Indicate sensor reading (a sweep over the grid)
        sweep = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.2, color=RED).move_to(p) for p in self.grid.values()])
        self.play(Create(sweep), run_time=1)
        self.play(FadeOut(sweep))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(BLUE)
        # Update belief: color change of dots
        self.play(
            *[dot.animate.set_color(GRAY) for dot in grid_group if dot.get_center()[0] < 3],
            *[dot.animate.set_color(BLUE) for dot in grid_group if dot.get_center()[0] >= 3]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(FadeIn(target_dot))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(Indicate(target_dot, color=YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)
